items.title: How close is the Hurontario LRT to being finished?
items.summary: The Hurontario LRT, also known as the Hazel McCallion Line, was supposed to be completed in the fall of 2024, but the pandemic and construction delays prevented that from happening. CBC’s Nav Nanwa updates us on the project and how close it is to completion.

items.title: Mississauga council adjusting committee structure for new term
items.summary: Mississauga councillors have voted to make multiple adjustments to the committee structure, which the mayor says is part of an effort to modernize how council functions.

items.title: Community outrage sparks judicial review of Mississauga cannabis store licence
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is seeking a judicial review of the province's decision to grant a retail licence to a cannabis store in Meadowvale Village, following backlash from residents who say they weren't consulted about it.

items.title: Peel Police Set to Detail New Home Invasion Probe Tied to Luxury Vehicle Thefts
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel police are set to release details of a new probe into home invasions across the GTA targeting luxury vehicles. Investigators say auto theft has dropped in Mississauga and Brampton in recent years, but it remains a top concern, especially when a home break-in is involved, since that puts residents at risk. The announcement follows a separate bust less than two weeks ago in which a dozen men face 231 combined charges over stolen luxury SUVs and other high-value vehicles taken from driveways across the GTA. Police say that ring moved the stolen vehicles out of Ontario within days, loading them into containers bound overseas from the Port of Montreal. The probe, led by Peel's commercial auto crime squad with the Canada Border Services Agency, turned up a broader criminal network across the region, investigators said.

items.title: Mississauga Councillor Says Malton Greenway Sees Eight Encampment Removals a Month
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga council voted unanimously on Nov. 25 to study improvements for the Malton Greenway after Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart said years of neglect and encampments have left residents afraid to use the trail. Hart told council and city staff that the two-kilometre park and trail in the city's north end is meant to connect people but currently cannot be used safely. She said the area has seen more encampments than resident activity over the past couple of years, with crews now removing roughly eight encampments a month. Hart's motion directs city staff to explore options for cleaning up and improving safety along the greenway. The councillor pointed to an incident the same morning in which a parks crew was called to clear garbage illegally dumped behind a nearby mall.

items.title: Erindale Development Would Replace Two Homes on Oneida Crescent With Eight
items.summary: According to insauga.com, residents spoke out against a proposal to replace two homes on Oneida Crescent in Mississauga's Erindale neighbourhood with eight new homes. The property at 2184 and 2194 Oneida Cres. would see one existing home demolished to make way for seven new homes, for a total of eight on the site, according to a report before the Planning and Development Committee. Four of the homes would be freehold, while the other four would be condominium detached homes built along a new common element road. The project requires both an Official Plan Amendment and a rezoning before it can proceed. Jim Levac, a partner with Glen Schnarr and Associates representing the applicant, told the committee on Nov. 23 that the proposal is not a large development and is a good fit for the neighbourhood. He said the design was intended to be compatible with the existing community.

items.title: Peel Public Health Issues Conditional Passes to Two Mississauga Restaurants
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, two Mississauga restaurants received conditional passes during recent inspections, meaning each had one or more infractions that needed correcting. Peel Public Health inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout establishments to ensure compliance with the Health Protection and Promotion Act, the health unit says. A green pass indicates full compliance, while a conditional pass flags violations inspectors found during a visit, according to Peel Region. One of the two restaurants, Spoon and Fork Corner at 1225 Dundas St., Unit 14B, was inspected on Nov. 18, Peel Public Health says. The health unit did not specify in its public summary which violations led to either restaurant's conditional pass.

items.title: Mississauga Man Wins $250,000 Scratch Ticket Prize at Local Rabba Store
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a Mississauga man identified only as Chris K. won $250,000 with a Golden Fortune scratch ticket bought at a Rabba Fine Foods on Heatherleigh Avenue in Mississauga. Chris told Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation officials he stopped at the store for coffee and decided to pick up a few extra tickets while he was there. He said he checked the tickets right away and was in shock when $250,000 flashed across the screen. Chris said he mostly plays scratch tickets and this was his first major lottery win, which he shared with his mother soon after. He told OLG he plans to use the winnings to pay some bills and treat his parents to a nice breakfast.
